rubrics.date: Rubricae generales 11 a and 15 (Vatican typical edition, p. [XII]), 20–21 and 24–25 (p. XIII), with the table at 91 (places 4, 16, 18 and 25) and 93 (p. XVII): every day of the week but Sunday is a feria (21); the ferias of Advent are of the second class from 17 to 23 December and on the Ember days of Advent, and otherwise of the third class (24–25); the Immaculate Conception and the second-class feasts of the universal Church are preferred to them, and a feria so impeded is commemorated (24, 25, 93). St Andrew's day is in Advent when the First Sunday of Advent, the Sunday on or nearest 30 November, precedes it (20); a Sunday of Advent is of the first class and is preferred to every feast but the Immaculate Conception (11 a, 15).
rubrics.scope: Observed in the Mass of the feast by the Collect, Secret and Postcommunion of the feria's own Mass, as its formulary assembles them: the ferias of Advent say the Mass of the preceding Sunday, and the Ember days of Advent have a Mass of their own (Rubricae generales 298–299, p. XXII), which this edition does not yet carry, so the commemoration of an Ember day is stated unavailable rather than said from the Sunday.
rubrics.rank: Rubricae generales 107–109 e (p. XVIII): the commemoration of a feria of Advent is privileged and is made in all Masses (108).
rubrics.admission: Rubricae generales 111 a and c and 434 a and c (pp. XVIII, XXXI): a first-class day, and a sung Mass that is not conventual, admit one privileged commemoration, and another second-class day one commemoration; 113–114 (p. XIX): a de Tempore commemoration comes first and the excess is omitted.
rubrics.conclusion: Rubricae generales 436–437 (p. XXXI): each commemoration oration follows the corresponding Mass oration under its own, separate conclusion; 480–481: only the last Secret's terminal is audible.
